phases.objective: Re-register the trusted issue-comment dispatcher under a fresh GitHub Actions path without changing its workflow bytes, public workflow name, permissions, exact-head checks, delegated writer, or no-secret boundary.

e2e_journeys.actor: repository contract maintainer and GitHub Actions workflow registry
e2e_journeys.entrypoint: Merge of a byte-equivalent dispatcher workflow move to the protected default branch
e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: GitHub receives a fresh workflow path for Governed Generated Artifact Refresh Dispatch while the stale path is absent and all trusted command, exact-head, writer-observation, publication, and fail-closed contracts remain enforced.
steps: Create the new workflow path from the exact existing dispatcher content.
Remove the stale workflow path in the same reviewable branch without force push.
Update active workflow-path references in tests and E2E evidence contracts.
Run the dispatcher workflow contract and bounded publisher contract.
After merge, issue one trusted exact-head refresh command and require an observed delegated writer run ID.
assertions: The workflow name remains Governed Generated Artifact Refresh Dispatch.
The retired workflow path is absent.
The new workflow remains issue_comment and workflow_dispatch only.
Permissions remain actions:write, contents:read, issues:write, and pull-requests:read, with no contents:write.
The dispatcher checks out trusted main without persisted credentials and never checks out candidate code.
The generated-artifact-refresh label, exact current PR head, trusted author association, and protected-branch rejection remain mandatory.
HTTP 204 alone is not accepted; passed evidence requires delegated_run_observed=true and a numeric delegated_run_id.

No generated file mutation, migration, deployment, Production mutation, provider call, credential access, external send, direct protected-branch write, or force push occurs in this re-registration PR.

phases.objective: Observe the first trusted command on the re-registered default-branch workflow publish a delegated writer run ID and start the exact-head writer.
Continue to fail closed for stale heads, missing labels, untrusted authors, protected branches, inactive writer state, rejected dispatch, and an unobserved delegated run.
This repository workflow registration repair performs no provider or deployment canary.
This repair grants no migration, runtime, deployment, provider, credential, or Production authority.
